artboards.title: The guard — a refresh never eats your typing

annotations.text:
WHAT THIS CHANGE IS

Live invalidation, and nothing else. One window saves, every other window re-reads itself. No refresh button, no "this page is out of date" banner.

IN: /ws endpoint, an in-process registry, a broadcast fired from the mutating routes, and a client that reconnects with backoff and reloads whole on reconnect.

OUT, deliberately: presence badges (needs a name from SSO), cursors, typing indicators, live co-editing of a sprint file.

COST: zero new dependencies — uvicorn[standard] already brings websockets, and FastAPI has WebSocket built in. One uvicorn worker, because the registry lives in process memory.

SETTLED

WHICH TABS FOLLOW — all of them. Project, Portfolio and Map re-read on a change, and the Sprint tab listens on the same socket with the same reload call (its own artboard shows the one carve-out: unsaved text is offered a reload, never given one).

PRESENCE — deferred until SSO supplies a name that cannot be typed.

STILL OPEN

1. THE FLASH. A row that changed under you washes indigo for 1.6s (the arrival-flash a jump already uses). The alternative is silence — the number simply differs from what you last looked at. Drawn: with the flash.

2. THE DROPPED BADGE. Nothing is drawn while the socket is live; a badge appears only when it is not. The alternative is to draw nothing ever and let it catch up quietly.

THE TRAP THIS AVOIDS

loadPlan() rebuilds the phase table. If it runs while your cursor is in a cell, that input is removed — and Chrome fires blur on a focused element that gets removed, which is the trap editor.js already documents. The blur handler is what saves the field.

So an unguarded live refresh does not merely interrupt you: it can save a half-typed value, or throw it away.

The rule: hold the refresh while an input inside the plan table has focus; run it on blur.

HOW THE SPRINT TAB LISTENS

It is the highest-collision surface in the app — autosave on blur, a 600ms debounce, a whole file per PUT — so it gains the most from listening and is the one place a blind reload would cost real work.

So the reload is conditional on one thing only: whether this page has anything unsaved.

CLEAN — reload, exactly like the other tabs.
DIRTY, SAVING, or already in conflict — do not reload. Raise the save bar's existing "Changed on disk" state and pause autosave, which is what a stale mtime does today at the next save. Same bar, same button, same refusal to decide whose version wins; it just arrives when the file changes instead of minutes later.

The picker's file list refreshes unconditionally — listing files touches nothing you are typing.

This needs a second broadcast the roadmap rows do not: POST/PUT on a sprint file announces {scope:"sprint", number:N}. The deliverable tick already rewrites markers in sprint files, so that write announces both.

HOW THIS PAIRS WITH WHAT SHIPPED TODAY

The row guard refuses a write whose expectation of a field has been overtaken. Its cost is that a refusal can arrive minutes after the value moved, because a page holds whatever it last loaded.

Live invalidation shortens that to a round trip: every window's loaded row is refreshed the moment someone writes, so the expectation it states is almost always current.

It does not replace the guard — a broadcast is a hint that may never arrive, and only the server-side check can actually refuse. They are freshness and refusal, and you want both.

WHY PRESENCE WAITS

The original plan had a display name typed once and kept in localStorage. That was dropped before it was built: a typed name is self-asserted, anyone can claim to be anyone, and presence that shows who is where is only worth drawing if the who is trustworthy.

So the name comes from the sign-in claim — which means SSO lands first, and SSO is blocked on questions for your Keycloak admin.

Nothing in the socket work has to change when it arrives: the connection is already there, and presence is a second message type on it.
